guard: `run ps --local` reads the revocation marker beside each run record and prints `revoked` whatever the record says, names the revoker and the reason under the table, and `revoke` says what the table will now show; the record itself is never rewritten. A marker the listing cannot read prints `unchecked` in the STATE column, its reason and the record's own state go to stderr, every other row still prints, and the command exits 1. A revoke with an empty by or reason is refused before the marker is written
why: THE DIRECTION IS A ROW THAT LOOKS HEALTHY. A revocation is a create-only marker in the
admission store and nothing rewrites the run record (SPEC 14.8); the record is written only by
a driver, so a driver that dies mid-run leaves `running` behind with nothing left to write
anything else. Neither surface is broken in a way anyone can see: the marker is correct, the
record is correct, and the table that reads only one of them prints a live row for a run that
will never run again. An operator counting capacity from it counts that row.
THE CONTROL IS MEASURED RATHER THAN MUTATED, and this is deliberate. The cell before the
revoke asserts the same run prints `running`, on the same table, through the same code path.
At 08cff353, the base this PR was first measured on, that control PASSED while the cell after
the revoke FAILED, which
is the only evidence that separates `this table reads the marker` from `this table happens to
print the word revoked`. A mutant that forced every row to `revoked` would redden an earlier
block's `with its state` cell first, so it would name the wrong line; the base measurement
answers the same question without that ambiguity.
MUTATION TWO CROSSES A PACKAGE BOUNDARY AND SO CARRIES ITS OWN COMMAND. The suite imports
`@cotal-ai/core` by package name, which resolves to `dist/`, so a mutation in `packages/core/src`
is invisible to it unless core is rebuilt first. It builds core before the suite and rebuilds
it after the restore, or the tree keeps a `dist/` compiled from the mutant.
MUTATIONS ONE AND TWO NAME THE SAME CELL, and the reason is worth writing down because the
issue predicted otherwise. #1621 expected that reading the admission key instead of the marker
key would make a live admission read as a revocation. It does not: `revocationSnapshot` is a
closed-field validator, so an admission record fails it, the read THROWS, and `ps` prints the
row as `unchecked`. Same cell, different mechanism, and the two are repaired differently: one is
a table that stopped looking, the other is a table looking in the wrong place and saying so.
THE UNCHECKED PATH HAS ITS OWN BLOCK, because it was graded by nothing when it printed the
record's own word. Block 10 writes a version-2 marker RAW (the exported writer validates, so an
unreadable marker has to be created past it) on a run held at a checkpoint, so its record really
reads `running`. One mutation per claim: the column, stdout staying free of the record's word,
the stderr line, the other rows, and the exit status. The exit status has a CONTROL in block 9,
where every marker was read, and the unconditional-exit mutant is the positive control that shows
that control can see a listing that always exits 1. The core mutant that swallows a failed read
grades the `readRunRevocation` contract that `no marker` and `could not look` are different
answers; it is measured here through the table, and on its own in the core twin below.
THE EMPTY-FIELD REFUSAL IS AT THE WRITER ONLY. The argument parser passes `--by ""` through as an
empty string, so the CLI could write a marker that rendered as `revoked by  ()`. The reader stays
tolerant: refusing an existing marker would make the run's admission unreadable, and an
unreadable admission also refuses the conclave cleanup a revoked run is still owed.
THE THREE CORE MUTATIONS HAVE TWINS IN packages/core/smoke/mutations/run-revocation-marker.json.
This suite imports `@cotal-ai/core` by name and builds it in the mutation's command, so
`mutation-coverage --gradable-only` refuses to grade them here, as it refuses
run-host-isolation.json for the same reason. `mutation-proof` still kills them here, which is
what shows the real command reaches them; the twins are graded where the contract is written.
NOT ASSERTED, and recorded rather than implied: the manager-hosted `run ps` has the same
defect at `implementations/runtime/src/run-host.ts` `list()`, which builds `RunListRow` from
the record alone. Fixing it needs a field on that served answer shape and a manager credential
that may read the admission bucket, which is a wider change than the local surface this issue
names, and it cannot be driven from this suite.

mutations.expectRed: ps prints revoked for it afterwards, whatever the record says
mutations.note: This is the shipped state before the fix, and it is what 08cff353, the base this PR was first measured on, printed: the row reads `running`, the local holder id, journal 0, with the marker sitting unread beside it.

mutations.find:
const marker = await readLeader(jsm, space, revocationKey(endpoint, runId));
  return marker === undefined ? undefined : revocationSnapshot(marker.value, runId);
mutations.replace:
const marker = await readLeader(jsm, space, admissionKey(endpoint, runId));
  return marker === undefined ? undefined : revocationSnapshot(marker.value, runId);
mutations.cell: ps prints revoked for it afterwards, whatever the record says
mutations.expectRed: ps prints revoked for it afterwards, whatever the record says
mutations.note: Measured rather than predicted: the admission record fails `revocationSnapshot`, so this does not report a live admission as a revocation, it makes the read throw. `ps` then prints the row as `unchecked`, which reddens the same cell for a different reason. It does so for EVERY row, so it is not the only red: measured by hand at 2243f4f0 it reddens eight cells. The first is block 2's `with its state`, and block 9's before-revoke control is among them. The named cell is the claim it breaks, not the first line it breaks. The anchor spans two lines because the host read beside it is byte-identical on its first line; a single-line target matched both and was refused as ambiguous.

mutations.expectRed: ...with the revoker and the reason under the table, since the columns carry neither
mutations.note: A state of `revoked` with no attribution anywhere sends the operator to a second command to learn who revoked it and why; the marker carries both and the columns carry neither.

mutations.name: revoke stops saying what the table will show
mutations.find: console.log(`run ps now lists ${runId} as revoked; the status record is left as its driver last wrote it`);
mutations.cell: ...and says what the table will now show, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart unnoticed
mutations.expectRed: ...and says what the table will now show, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart unnoticed
mutations.note: The acknowledgement and the table disagreed for as long as one of them never read the marker. Saying it at the moment of the revoke is what makes a future divergence visible to the person who caused it.
